failure_analysis: No hidden cases failed in any trial. The rendered docs did well on the exact decision points this task required: the WP_HTML_Tag_Processor overview says to use the Tag Processor for flat, position-based tag/class/attribute edits and byte-precise preservation; the Usage section shows construction with new WP_HTML_Tag_Processor($html); Finding tags documents next_tag('img'); next_tag() explicitly states ASCII case-insensitive tag-name matching, skipping tag-like text inside comments/raw-text sections, and not matching incomplete trailing tags; add_class() states that it creates a class attribute, appends to existing classes without reordering, and avoids duplicates; get_updated_html() states that queued class edits are read back there and untouched bytes are preserved. Near-misses were also covered: the candidates did not check add_class()'s return value, but the docs say this is unnecessary in the usual add-then-get_updated_html flow; they relied on incomplete input remaining unchanged, and the next_tag()/get_updated_html contracts together support that behavior.
